topic: Taxonomic Aids: Herbaria, Museums, Botanical Gardens and Keys
title: Why Keep a Pressed Leaf? Explained Simply | PUC Biology Class 11
description:
Diya finds a dried leaf pressed between the pages of her grandfather's old book and asks why anyone would keep a dead leaf for years. Scientists keep huge collections like this on purpose: they are taxonomic aids, the tools that help us identify and name living things.

You will see a herbarium sheet built and labelled, then a zoom ladder from the sheet to its label (date, place, English, local and botanical names, family, collector) to the cupboard where sheets are stored in order. Watch one sheet being made stage by stage (collect, press, dry, mount, label and store), meet botanical gardens (Kew, Howrah, Lucknow), museums and zoological parks, compare a herbarium with a botanical garden, and learn to use a key with couplets and leads by running four animals through one. Then the exam trap, an original NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself. Note: this topic is not in the current rationalised NCERT text.

This is Episode 9 of our PUC Biology series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11 and NEET students.
